gaps.sentence: She ___ admitted that she had made a mistake (HONEST).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ly forms adverbs: honestly modifies the verb 'admitted'.

gaps.sentence: He answered all the questions with great ___ (CONFIDENT).
gaps.explanation: 'Great' needs a noun: confidence. 'Confident' is the adjective.

gaps.sentence: The soup tastes a bit ___ ; add some salt (TASTE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -less means without: tasteless explains why salt is needed. An adjective follows 'tastes'.

gaps.sentence: The crowd waited ___ for the gates to open (PATIENT).
gaps.explanation: An adverb modifies the verb 'waited': patiently. 'Patients' are people in hospital.

gaps.sentence: We must take ___ for our own health (RESPONSIBLE).
gaps.explanation: 'Take responsibility for something' is the fixed phrase; the -ity noun is needed.

gaps.sentence: The crisis could ___ the economic situation (WORSE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -en forms the verb: worsen means to make worse. A base verb follows 'could'.

gaps.sentence: The trip gave us a lot of ___ (PLEASE).
gaps.explanation: 'A lot of' needs a noun: pleasure (note the irregular spelling).

gaps.sentence: It was ___ of you to double-check the figures (SENSE).
gaps.explanation: 'It was sensible of you to do something' praises good judgement; 'sensitive' means easily affected.
